How to act on this result

  • Search all fields

EXIF DETAILS

What can this EXIF viewer show?

This EXIF viewer reads the information a photo can carry beyond its pixels. When those fields are present, you can check the camera model, lens, shutter speed, aperture, ISO, date taken, GPS coordinates, orientation, software, and related capture notes. It also surfaces nearby XMP and IPTC records, helping you understand how an image was captured, edited, exported, or prepared for sharing—all locally in your browser.

WHY IT MATTERS

Why view file metadata?

Metadata can expose private details, explain how a file was made, and save time when you need technical facts.

Frequently asked questions

Is this metadata viewer safe to use?

The file is processed inside this browser tab. ViewExif has no upload endpoint, account, or server-side parser for your selected file.

What EXIF data can this viewer read?

When those fields are present, it can read camera model, lens, ISO, aperture, shutter speed, timestamps, GPS coordinates, orientation, XMP, IPTC, and other available EXIF and file metadata.

Can this reveal where a photo was taken?

If the image contains usable GPS coordinates, the report shows them. Many files contain no location, and metadata can be removed or changed.

Can metadata be wrong?

Yes. Dates, locations, camera labels, authors, and every other editable field can be stale, missing, or deliberately changed.

Can metadata restore blurred or redacted parts of an image?

No. Metadata inspection does not reconstruct pixels. It can only reveal stored fields or an embedded preview that is already inside the file.
